sections.h2: Where in Delta County are deeds recorded?
sections.html:
Every deed in the county is recorded in Escanaba. The Register of Deeds works from the county building at 310 Ludington Street, open from eight to four, and the county line is (906) 789-5100, with a fax at (906) 789-5179.

That holds whether the house stands in Escanaba, in Gladstone, in the village of Garden, or out in a township near Rapid River or Rock. Call ahead about anything unusual. Bring the original signed deed and the fee, and ask whether the counter takes cards.

The office follows the statewide schedule in MCL 600.2567, which applies unless a charter county sets its own. Under it a deed is $30 to record whatever the page count.

Recording fees for an Escanaba closing
ServiceFee
Recording one document$30.00
Each additional instrument in an assignment or discharge$3.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00
Records search on request$0.50 for each year, minimum $5
Filing another paper$1.00

Payment is due when you hand the paper to the clerk. An electronic filing that is also paid electronically can settle within one business day under the statute. Ask the office whether it accepts e-recording and through which vendors. Bring along a list of everything being recorded so the clerk can quote one total.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes out of a Delta County seller's proceeds?
sections.html:
Expect a deduction at closing. Delta County sellers owe a state tax of $3.75 plus a county tax of $0.55, and both are counted per $500 of price. Round any remainder up to a whole $500. The county rate is in MCL 207.504. Liability sits with the seller under MCL 207.523. Checks go to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed reaches the buyer.

Several kinds of transfer owe no state tax:

  • anything under $100;
  • security instruments;
  • land contracts that hold back title until paid;
  • conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.

MCL 207.505 gives the county a shorter list of exemptions. Deeding a house to your daughter, say, can skip the state portion yet still draw the county portion. Check with the register about your own deed before signing.

Print the sale value on the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it. Did tax get paid on a sale that turned out to be exempt? The seller, or a buyer who paid for the seller, may apply to the Department of Treasury for a refund.

sections.h2: Which deeds need a treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
Most sale deeds do. Under MCL 211.135 the register must hold a deed, plat or land contract until the treasurer certifies tax liens and tax titles and confirms that five years of taxes are paid.

Excused from certification: quitclaims and other conveyances without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds, and some state tax deeds. The same treasurer holds county funds, collects delinquent property taxes and runs the yearly tax sale for the State Treasury.

Before you pick a closing date, ask the treasurer what the certificate costs and how fast it is issued.

The Delta County Equalization office serves title agents and appraisers. Its price list shows a $5 Equalization Report, a $15 Apportionment Report listing millage rates, and $15 for taxable value broken out by school district or township. Database copies run $1 a page and simple maps $2.

A single house is different. For its assessed and taxable value, contact the assessor in the city or township where it sits. A buyer estimating the first tax bill will want those two numbers and the millage rate. If you are a seller, having them ready when you list answers the first question an interested buyer is likely to ask about carrying costs.

sections.h2: Recording a Delta County sale, start to finish
sections.html:
Five steps carry a sale through. An attorney or title company drafts the deed and every seller signs, printing a name beneath the signature. A notary, judge or court clerk then acknowledges those signatures. If the deed warrants title, the treasurer's certificate comes next. The closing agent calculates the transfer tax on the full price and sets aside the recording fee. Last, the package reaches 310 Ludington Street in Escanaba, and the register records it.

What arrives at the counter should be the signed original, never a photocopy, plus the fee and any certificate. A buyer paying cash has no lender, so no mortgage gets recorded and the deed with its fees is the entire package. That keeps the visit brief.

Unpaid property tax is what most often holds up a deed. No certificate issues while a lien or balance is outstanding, and a warranty deed sits at the register until one arrives. Ask for a written payoff figure before you fix a closing date, and let the closing agent pay it from what you receive at the sale. The certificate then comes back clean, with no second trip to the office.

Raise the tax question with your closing agent the day you accept an offer. A cash buyer will want these loose ends tied up well before closing, and a clear certificate is one less thing to negotiate.

sections.h2: Delta County housing at a glance
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied house here is valued at $157,100. Median rent is $692 and median household income is $57,809. Owners live in 82.0% of occupied homes. The county has about 36,582 residents spread over 1,171 square miles of land, so parcels range from city lots in Escanaba and Gladstone to farms and forest acreage. Prices and what a buyer expects will differ across that range, and the recording steps above stay the same for all of it.

For a seller the practical upshot is variety. A lakeside cottage near Escanaba, a house in Gladstone and forty acres near Garden call for different disclosures, surveys and legal descriptions, but all three travel to the same counter on Ludington Street for recording.

sections.h2: What formatting does a Delta County deed need?
sections.html:
One recording format applies across Michigan under MCL 565.201, and the Escanaba office enforces these items.

  • Signatures in ink, each followed by a printed name, with the same spelling used in the deed body and the notary block.
  • A street address for every party, and the drafter's name with a way to reach them.
  • For a deed signed in Michigan, an acknowledgment taken by a notary, judge or court clerk.
  • 2.5 inches left blank at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp.
  • A Social Security number, if shown, cut down to its last four digits.

Clerks do not draft deeds or offer legal advice. Inherited a house? Your title company can tell you whether a death certificate or court order must be recorded first, and finding out early keeps an estate sale moving.

faqs.q: How much does the Delta County register charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, per MCL 600.2567. A release naming several instruments adds $3 for each extra, and certifying a recorded paper costs $5.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Delta County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The state rate is $3.75 and the county rate 55 cents for every $500 slice, payable to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: Do deeds for Gladstone and Garden homes go to Escanaba?
faqs.a: Yes. The register at 310 Ludington Street records for the entire county, including both cities and the village.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed exempt from the treasurer's certificate in Delta County?
faqs.a: Yes, when it has no warranty covenants. A warranty deed or land contract must carry the certificate before the register will accept it.

faqs.q: What are the register's hours in Escanaba?
faqs.a: Eight to four. Telephone (906) 789-5100 to confirm holiday closures.
